questions.q:
The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 was defeated in the Lok Sabha in April 2026. In this context, which of the following statements are correct?
1. The Bill had the support of more than half of the total membership of the House but not of two-thirds of the members present and voting.
2. A Bill of this kind cannot be introduced in a State Legislature.
3. After its defeat, the President could have summoned a joint sitting of both Houses to pass it.
4. The Bill could be introduced only on the prior recommendation of the President.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: With 528 present, the Bill won 298 votes against 230: above half of the House's strength, yet short of the 352 that two-thirds of those present and voting required, so statement 1 is correct. Under Article 368 an amendment Bill can start only in either House of Parliament, never in a State Legislature, so statement 2 is correct. The joint sitting under Article 108 does not apply to amendment Bills, and no prior Presidential recommendation is needed for them, so statements 3 and 4 are wrong.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 9-10; Shankar IAS pp. 3-6; Articles 108 and 368 are static

questions.q:
With reference to the bills withdrawn along with the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The Delimitation Bill, 2026 would have replaced the Delimitation Act, 2002 and provided for a Commission headed by a sitting or retired Supreme Court judge.
2. The Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 would have extended the changes to Delhi, Puducherry and Ladakh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Delimitation Bill was to repeal the 2002 Act, have the Union constitute a Commission chaired by a serving or former Supreme Court judge, and use the latest Census published when the Commission is formed, which is 2011. Statement 2 is wrong because the parallel Union Territories Bill covered Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir, the UTs with their own legislatures. Ladakh, a Union Territory without a legislature, was not covered. Both Bills were withdrawn after the amendment failed.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 9-10; Shankar IAS pp. 3-6
questions.it: Delimitation Bill and UT Laws Bill

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes what the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 sought to do with Article 82?
o: Shift the task of readjusting constituencies from a Delimitation Commission to the Election Commission of India
Allow the orders of the Delimitation Commission to be challenged before the High Courts
Extend the use of the 1971 population figures for allotting Lok Sabha seats until the first Census after 2031
Delete the proviso that ties the next readjustment of seats to the first Census taken after 2026, so that the 2011 Census could be used
questions.e: Article 82 requires readjustment of seats after each Census, but its third proviso postpones this until figures of the first Census taken after 2026 are published. The 2026 Bill proposed deleting that proviso so that delimitation could rest on the 2011 Census and women's reservation could start by the 2029 election. It did not extend the 1971 freeze, which it would actually have ended. It kept a Commission model, and it did not open Commission orders to court challenge.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 9-10; Shankar IAS pp. 3-6; Article 82 proviso is static

questions.q:
The 106th Constitutional Amendment (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam), 2023 was at the centre of the April 2026 amendment debate. With reference to it, consider the following statements:
1. Its reservation extends to the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi.
2. Its reservation does not extend to the Rajya Sabha or to the State Legislative Councils.
3. Seats reserved for women are to be rotated after each subsequent delimitation.
4. The reservation is set for fifteen years from its commencement, which Parliament may extend by law.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. The Amendment changed Article 239AA so that Delhi's Assembly also reserves one-third of seats for women. Only directly elected houses are covered, so the Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils are outside it. Article 334A provides that reserved seats rotate after each later delimitation, and sets a fifteen-year span that Parliament may extend by law. The catch is that the reservation starts only after delimitation on a fresh Census, the link the 2026 Bill tried to change.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 9-10; Shankar IAS pp. 3-6; Articles 239AA and 334A are static

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II, with reference to the framework for the Census in India:
List-I
A. Constitutional basis
B. Statute
C. Conducting office
D. Subordinate rules
List-II
1. Census Rules, 1990
2. Entry 69 of the Union List
3. Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, Ministry of Home Affairs
4. Census Act, 1948
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Census is a Union subject: Entry 69 of the Union List, read with Article 246, gives Parliament the power. The Census Act, 1948 gives the statutory mandate, and the Census Rules, 1990 fill in the procedure. The exercise is run by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, which sits under the Home Ministry, not under the Statistics Ministry that runs NSO surveys. Census 2027 will be India's sixteenth Census and the eighth since Independence.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 7-9; Seventh Schedule entry is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Census of 1881 is regarded as the first synchronous Census of India.
Statement-II: The population counts made between 1865 and 1872 were carried out in different regions at different times.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, and the second explains the first. Counts between 1865 and 1872 were not held at the same time across British India, so they cannot be treated as one national snapshot. In 1881, under Census Commissioner W.C. Plowden, the whole country was counted together for the first time, and the Census was then held every ten years without a break until the pandemic delayed the 2021 round. Earlier records such as the Arthashastra and the Ain-i-Akbari are counts for taxation and administration.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 7-9

questions.q:
In April 2026 the Supreme Court dealt with the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal. In this context, consider the following statements:
1. The Election Commission's control over the preparation of electoral rolls flows from Article 324.
2. The Court invoked Article 142 to provide an appeal route through tribunals.
3. The preparation of electoral rolls is governed by the Representation of the People Act, 1950, while the conduct of elections falls under the 1951 Act.
4. The Court directed that all deleted names be restored to the rolls until the appeals were decided.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 324 vests superintendence of rolls and elections in the Commission. Statement 2 is correct, since Article 142 lets the Court pass orders for complete justice, here outside the statutory route. Statement 3 is correct: the 1950 Act deals with rolls and the 1951 Act with conduct of elections. Statement 4 is wrong: the order of 6 April let about 27 lakh deletions stand through a supplementary list and sent aggrieved voters to newly set-up appellate tribunals.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 26-27; Article 324 and the RP Acts are static

questions.q:
In April 2026 a nominated member was elected Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha for a third consecutive term. With reference to the office of Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, consider the following statements:
1. The Deputy Chairman submits his resignation in writing to the President.
2. A nominated member is eligible for the office, since Article 89 requires only that the person be a member of the House.
3. The Deputy Chairman may be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a majority of all the then members of the House.
4. While presiding, the Deputy Chairman does not vote in the first instance but has a casting vote in case of a tie.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Article 89 lets the Council choose its Deputy Chairman from among its members, elected or nominated, which is how a nominated member won a third term. Article 90 allows removal by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members, after fourteen days' notice. Under Article 100 the person presiding votes only to break a tie. Statement 1 is wrong: the Deputy Chairman resigns by writing addressed to the Chairman, not to the President.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 11; Articles 89, 90 and 100 are static

questions.q:
The first conference of the India Region of the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA) was held in April 2026. With reference to the CPA, which of the following statements are correct?
1. Its membership is confined to the national parliaments of Commonwealth countries.
2. It traces its origin to 1911 and is headquartered in London.
3. It publishes the journal 'The Parliamentarian'.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The CPA, founded in 1911 and based in London, works to strengthen parliamentary democracy and good governance, and it publishes 'The Parliamentarian'. Statement 1 is wrong because its roughly 180 branches include state and provincial legislatures as well as national parliaments, grouped into nine geographic regions, India being one of them. This is why a CPA India Region meeting brings together Parliament and the State legislatures.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 12

questions.q:
The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026 was passed by Parliament, the Rajya Sabha clearing it on 2 April 2026. With reference to its scheme, consider the following statements:
1. It sets out a graded response of an advisory first, a warning next and a civil penalty for later contraventions.
2. It provides for improvement notices under the Legal Metrology Act so that a lapse can be corrected before a penalty is imposed.
3. It moves offences of fraud and threats to public safety out of the criminal courts to adjudicating officers.
4. It builds in an automatic periodic increase in the fines it sets.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: the Bill uses a graded response, improvement notices under the Legal Metrology Act, and a 10 per cent rise in the minimum fine every three years so penalties do not erode. Statement 3 is wrong. The Bill's guiding idea is proportionality: criminal sanctions are kept for fraud, wilful evasion and threats to public safety, while paperwork and procedural lapses move to civil penalties decided by adjudicating officers, with appeals under fixed timelines.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 5-7; Shankar IAS pp. 24-25; Rajya Sabha passage on 2 April 2026 is outside the notes (they say Lok Sabha only)

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes a 'Special Intensive Revision' of electoral rolls, such as the one in West Bengal that reached the Supreme Court in April 2026?
o: The routine annual summary revision of rolls with 1 January as the qualifying date
An extraordinary, verification-based revision by the Election Commission that goes beyond routine periodic revisions
A redrawing of Assembly constituency boundaries by the Delimitation Commission
A continuous updating of rolls through online applications between two elections
questions.e: An SIR is a special drive in which the Election Commission re-verifies the existing roll, here with software flags of 'logical discrepancy', observers and layered scrutiny, rather than merely adding and deleting names as in the routine summary revision or continuous updating. It is unrelated to delimitation, which redraws boundaries. In West Bengal it led to about 27 lakh deletions, close to 5 per cent of electors, which drew criticism because the roll had shown no clear sign of inflation.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 26-27

questions.q: Under the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, whose Rules were notified in April 2026, a game is treated as an 'online money game' chiefly on which one of the following grounds?
o: It is a game of chance rather than a game of skill
Its servers or operators are located outside India
The user pays a fee or stakes money in the expectation of winning money, whether the game rests on skill, chance or both
It has more registered users than a threshold notified by the Centre
questions.e: The 2025 Act moved away from the old skill-versus-chance test that courts had used for decades. A game becomes an online money game when users pay fees or deposit stakes expecting monetary or other enrichment, whatever the mix of skill and chance; such games are prohibited, while e-sports and social games are promoted. Location of servers and size of user base are factors the Centre may weigh when notifying games for registration, not the test for a money game.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 10-11; definition in the 2025 Act is static

questions.q: In the debate on 'trust-based governance' that accompanied the Jan Vishwas Bill, 2026, the argument that high-trust societies tend to be more economically advanced is associated with which one of the following?
questions.e: Francis Fukuyama, in his book on trust, argued that societies with high social trust build large organisations and prosper more easily, and the 2026 debate cited him for this link. Gunnar Myrdal is known for the idea of the 'soft state' in South Asia, a governance argument that can look similar. Douglass North wrote on institutions and transaction costs, and Amartya Sen on capabilities. The OECD defines trust as a belief that a person or institution will act in line with expectations of positive behaviour.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 5-7

questions.q:
The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 was introduced in Parliament in March 2026. With reference to the Act and the Bill as introduced, consider the following statements:
1. The Bill reduces the maximum term of imprisonment for offences under the Act.
2. The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010 is administered by the Ministry of Home Affairs.
3. Registration under the Act is valid for five years and must be renewed.
4. The Bill provides for a designated authority to take over assets created with foreign contribution once an organisation's registration ceases.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. The Bill cuts the maximum jail term from five years to one, a decriminalising signal. The Home Ministry is the nodal ministry for the 2010 Act, and registration lasts five years and must be renewed; over 18,000 NGOs have lost licences since 2015. The proposed designated authority, with powers like a civil court, would manage, transfer or sell assets created from foreign funds when registration is suspended, cancelled or expires, filling a gap in the 2010 Act.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 32-34; introduction in March 2026 is outside the notes (they say 'deferred')

questions.q:
The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026 were notified in April 2026. With reference to them, consider the following statements:
1. A user's complaint must first go to the online game service provider before it can be taken to the Online Gaming Authority of India.
2. Every online social game must be registered with the Authority before it is offered.
3. An appeal against the Authority's decision on a grievance lies with the Secretary of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
4. A game found to be an online money game can still be registered as an e-sport if it rests mainly on skill.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 4 are not correct. Registration is not universal: it is required for e-sports and for those games the Centre notifies on grounds of risk, scale or origin. A game found to be an online money game cannot be recognised as an e-sport, however much skill it involves, since the Act bans money games while promoting e-sports. Statements 1 and 3 are correct: a complaint goes first to the service provider, then to the Online Gaming Authority of India, and finally to the Secretary, MeitY, each stage within 30 days.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 10-11; three-stage grievance path checked against the notified Rules (PIB, Drishti, April 2026); the notes' 'two-tier' label is not tested

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 drew criticism on grounds of federalism.
Statement-II: The Bill requires prior approval of the Central Government before an offence under the Act is investigated, including by State agencies.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and linked. Police and public order are State subjects, yet the Bill makes any investigation of an FCRA offence wait for the Centre's nod, so State police or agencies cannot act on their own. Critics called this an intrusion on State powers; leaders from Tamil Nadu and Kerala also voiced fears for minority institutions, and others for NGO autonomy. The Catholic Bishops' Conference of India described the Bill as executive overreach.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 32-34

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes the AI Governance and Economic Group (AIGEG) constituted in April 2026?
o: A committee of the Reserve Bank of India on risks to banks from frontier AI models
An inter-ministerial body set up by MeitY and chaired by the Minister of Electronics and IT, supported by a Technology and Policy Expert Committee
A statutory regulator under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, chaired by the Chairperson of the Data Protection Board
A NITI Aayog body chaired by its Chief Executive Officer to fund AI start-ups under the IndiaAI Mission
questions.e: AIGEG is MeitY's ten-member inter-ministerial group, chaired by the Minister of Electronics and IT with the Minister of State as vice-chair, and including the Principal Scientific Adviser, the Chief Economic Adviser and NITI Aayog's CEO. A Technology and Policy Expert Committee advises it on risks and gaps. It is not a statutory data regulator or a funding body, and it should not be confused with the banking panel formed to study frontier-AI risk to the financial sector.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 9; glossary 13.8

questions.q:
With reference to the 'key functionaries' of an organisation under the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The definition would include the Karta of a Hindu Undivided Family and members of a governing body.
2. A key functionary would be liable for an offence by the organisation even if he shows that he exercised due diligence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Bill widens the term to cover trustees, partners, governing-body members, the Karta of a Hindu Undivided Family and anyone who manages or controls the body. Statement 2 is wrong. Such persons are presumed liable for the organisation's offences, but the presumption can be rebutted by showing that the offence occurred without their knowledge or that they exercised due diligence. Critics still fear the reverse burden will chill voluntary work.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 32-34

questions.q:
With reference to India's approach to artificial intelligence, consider the following pairs:
Initiative : Associated feature
1. National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence (2018) : 'AI for All', prepared by NITI Aayog
2. India AI Governance Guidelines : Seven guiding principles called 'sutras'
3. IndiaAI Mission : Implemented by the Ministry of Science and Technology
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pair 1 is correct: NITI Aayog's 2018 strategy carried the slogan 'AI for All' and stressed inclusive growth. Pair 2 is correct: the Guidelines rest on seven sutras such as trust, people first, accountability, understandability and safety, and they called for a whole-of-government approach that AIGEG now gives effect to. Pair 3 is wrong: the IndiaAI Mission is run under MeitY, not the Science and Technology Ministry, which is why MeitY anchors AI governance.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 9; IndiaAI Mission under MeitY is static

questions.q:
The debate on the tenure of the Prime Minister in April 2026 turned on Article 75. With reference to the office of Prime Minister, consider the following statements:
1. The Prime Minister may be a member of either House of Parliament.
2. A person who is not a member of either House may be appointed Prime Minister for up to six months.
3. The Prime Minister holds office during the pleasure of the President.
4. The Constitution requires the President to appoint the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha as Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Article 75 lets the President appoint a member of either House, and a non-member may be appointed if elected within six months. Office is held during the President's pleasure, which in practice means while the Lok Sabha majority lasts. Statement 4 is wrong: the Constitution lays down no selection procedure; choosing the leader of the majority party or coalition is a convention, and in a hung House the President uses discretion.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 30-32; Article 75 is static

questions.q: In the April 2026 debate on executive tenure, Ivor Jennings' test was cited to show that India has a convention against a third presidential term. Jennings' test asks which one of the following?
o: Whether the practice has lasted fifty years, been followed by every office-holder and been recorded in official manuals
Whether the rule is enforceable in court, supported by the executive and approved by a referendum
Whether the practice is written into a statute, upheld by a court and accepted by Parliament
Whether there are precedents, whether those involved believed they were bound by a rule, and whether there is a reason for the rule
questions.e: Ivor Jennings, in 'The Law and the Constitution', said a convention exists if there are precedents, the actors believe they are bound by a rule, and there is a good reason for it. Conventions are not written into statute or enforced by courts, which is why choices built on statute, courts or referendum are wrong. India's practice that no President serves more than two terms meets the test, so the mainly formal office is bound by a convention while the Prime Minister faces no limit except elections.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 30-32

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Constituent Assembly did not fix a limit on the number of terms a Prime Minister may serve.
Statement-II: B.R. Ambedkar argued that the daily assessment of the executive by Parliament is a stronger check than a periodic assessment by voters.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, and the second gives the reason for the first. Ambedkar told the Assembly in 1948 that questions, adjournment motions and no-confidence motions keep the executive answerable every day, which makes a fixed-term limit less needed. Critics now argue that the anti-defection law has blunted this daily check, since ruling-party members cannot vote against their own government without risking disqualification, so elections must carry more of the load.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 30-32

questions.q:
Justice Yashwant Varma resigned in April 2026 while proceedings for his removal were under way. With reference to the removal of judges of the higher judiciary, consider the following statements:
1. The grounds for removal are proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
2. A judge of the Supreme Court was removed from office after a motion moved in 1993.
3. The committee that investigates the charges is constituted by the Chief Justice of India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct: Article 124(4), applied to High Court judges by Article 218, allows removal for proved misbehaviour or incapacity. Statement 2 is wrong: the 1993 motion against Justice V. Ramaswami failed in the Lok Sabha, and no judge has ever been removed. Statement 3 is wrong: under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 the Speaker or Chairman admits the motion and constitutes the three-member committee. If it finds guilt, each House must pass the motion by special majority before the President orders removal.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 12; Ramaswami motion is static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Item : Associated with
1. Fifty-second Constitutional Amendment, 1985 : Insertion of the Tenth Schedule
2. Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992) : Upholding of the anti-defection law
3. Twenty-second Amendment to the US Constitution : Limit of two terms for the President after Franklin Roosevelt's four wins
4. Margaret Thatcher's exit in 1990 : Removal of a leader by her own party's MPs
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four pairs are correct. The 52nd Amendment added the Tenth Schedule, which disqualifies members who defy the party whip, and Kihoto Hollohan upheld it while making the Speaker's decision open to judicial review. The US adopted its 22nd Amendment in 1951 after Roosevelt's four terms. In the Westminster model there is no term limit, but a party can remove its own leader, as Conservative MPs did to Thatcher. Indian parties lack such a challenge mechanism, which the tenure debate highlights.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 30-32

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II, with reference to the law on judicial recusal in India:
List-I
A. Manak Lal v. Dr. Prem Chand (1957)
B. Ranjit Thakur v. Union of India (1987)
C. State of West Bengal v. Shivananda Pathak (1998)
D. Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (2015)
List-II
1. Bias as a state of mind that makes a judge unable to decide impartially
2. A judge refused to step aside on the doctrine of necessity
3. The test is a reasonable apprehension of bias, not a remote possibility
4. Pecuniary interest disqualifies a judge automatically
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Manak Lal held that a pecuniary interest disqualifies a judge without more and moved the law towards a real likelihood of bias. Ranjit Thakur set the test of reasonable apprehension in the mind of a fair-minded party. Shivananda Pathak described bias as a mental condition that prevents impartial judgment. In the NJAC case, Justice J.S. Khehar refused to recuse because the conflict touched every judge alike and no other forum existed, invoking the doctrine of necessity.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 12; Shankar IAS pp. 36-38

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In the NJAC case of 2015, Justice J.S. Khehar declined a request that he recuse himself.
Statement-II: The doctrine of necessity allows a judge with an interest to hear a case when no other judge or forum is available.
Statement-III: Justice Kurian Joseph held that a judge who recuses has no duty to state reasons.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of Statements II and III is correct and that one explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: a future Chief Justice, Khehar was asked to step aside from the challenge to the NJAC Act, 2014 and refused. Statement-II is correct and explains why: every judge shared the same interest and no other forum could hear the case. Statement-III is wrong: Justice Kurian Joseph, concurring, said a judge who recuses should disclose reasons as part of the transparency owed under the oath in the Third Schedule. The same reasoning now surrounds the challenge to the Election Commissioners Act, 2023.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 36-38; Third Schedule is static

questions.q:
Recusal of judges came into focus in April 2026 when the Chief Justice of India stepped away from a case. With reference to recusal, consider the following statements:
1. Recusal by judges of the Supreme Court is regulated by a parliamentary statute.
2. Recusal rests chiefly on the principle that no person should be condemned unheard.
3. A party to the case can compel a judge to recuse.
4. In the United States, federal law requires a judge to step aside whenever his impartiality might reasonably be questioned.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 4 is correct: Section 455 of Title 28 of the US Code makes disqualification mandatory where impartiality might reasonably be questioned. Statement 1 is wrong: India has no recusal statute; practice and case law govern it. Statement 2 is wrong: recusal flows from the rule against bias, nemo judex in causa sua, while 'no one should be condemned unheard' is audi alteram partem, the other limb of natural justice. Statement 3 is wrong: a party may ask, but the decision rests on the judge's conscience.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 12; Shankar IAS pp. 36-38

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Challenges to the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023 place a shared conflict of interest on judges of the Supreme Court.
Statement-II: Under that Act, the Chief Justice of India is a member of the committee that selects the Election Commissioners.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the case asks whether the Chief Justice should sit on the selection panel, and since every judge is a possible future Chief Justice under the seniority convention, the conflict is collective; two successive Chief Justices have recused. Statement-II is wrong: the 2023 Act set up a committee of the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister, leaving out the Chief Justice. That exclusion is the heart of the challenge.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 36-38; composition under the 2023 Act is static

questions.q:
Recusal by judges, discussed widely in April 2026, has no statute in India and rests on practice. Which of the following are commonly accepted grounds on which a judge steps aside?
1. The judge holds shares in a company that is a party to the case.
2. The judge earlier had a professional association with one of the parties.
3. The appeal before the Supreme Court is against a judgment the judge delivered while in a High Court.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: All three are standard grounds. A pecuniary interest such as shareholding in a litigant disqualifies a judge outright, as the NJAC judgment of 2015 restated. Prior association with a party, for instance as its lawyer, raises a reasonable apprehension of bias. A judge also does not sit in appeal over his own High Court judgment. All of these flow from nemo judex in causa sua. The decision still rests with the judge, and India has no review mechanism for it.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 12; Shankar IAS pp. 36-38

questions.q:
The Supreme Court acted against an NCERT Class 8 textbook chapter in 2026. With reference to contempt of court under the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, consider the following statements:
1. Wilful breach of an undertaking given to a court is criminal contempt.
2. 'Scandalising the court' is a form of civil contempt.
3. Fair comment on the merits of a case that has been heard and finally decided is punishable as contempt.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. Civil contempt covers wilful disobedience of a court's order and wilful breach of an undertaking given to it, so statement 1 is wrong. Scandalising or lowering the authority of a court, along with obstructing justice, is criminal contempt, so statement 2 is wrong. Section 5 of the 1971 Act protects fair comment on a case heard and finally decided, so statement 3 is wrong. Judges such as Gajendragadkar urged that the power be used sparingly.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 27-30; definitions and Section 5 of the 1971 Act are static

questions.q:
In April 2026 the Punjab and Haryana High Court restated the law on promotion in public service. With reference to this law, consider the following statements:
1. Promotion is a fundamental right of every eligible government employee under Article 16(1).
2. In Bihar State Electricity Board v. Dharamdeo Das (2024), the Supreme Court held that an employee gains a vested right to promotion from the date the vacancy arises.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. Promotion itself is not a fundamental right, since it depends on vacancies, merit and rules; what Articles 14 and 16(1) protect is the right to be considered for promotion by those in the zone of consideration. In Dharamdeo Das (2024) the Supreme Court said the opposite of statement 2: there is no vested right to promotion from the date of the vacancy, and delay alone does not earn retrospective promotion.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 34-36

questions.q:
NCERT was declared a deemed-to-be university in April 2026. With reference to this, consider the following statements:
1. Deemed-university status is conferred by the Central Government on the advice of the University Grants Commission.
2. NCERT was set up in 1961 and works under the Ministry of Education.
3. Under the National Education Policy 2020, NCERT is the nodal agency for National Curriculum Frameworks covering early childhood, school and adult education.
4. NCERT is registered as a society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956 lets the Centre, on the Commission's advice, declare an institution deemed to be a university. NCERT, set up in 1961 as an autonomous society registered under the 1860 Act and working under the Education Ministry, now gains university standing for its own programmes. NEP 2020 makes it the nodal agency for curriculum frameworks for early childhood care and education, school education and adult education.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 12-13; UGC Act and NCERT's society status are static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs, with reference to the law on promotion in public service:
Case or court : Point
1. Ajit Singh v. State of Punjab (1999) : A Constitution Bench treated the right to be considered for promotion as a fundamental right
2. Kulwant Singh case, Punjab and Haryana High Court (2026) : Notional promotion with retrospective effect and Departmental Promotion Committee meetings every three months
3. Manipur High Court (2022) : Faster Departmental Promotion Committees for senior lecturers nearing retirement
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Ajit Singh made denial of consideration a breach of Article 16(1). In the Kulwant Singh case a junior engineer was kept out of the DPC because his diploma came through distance learning, though the amended rules exempted serving staff; the court ordered notional promotion and quarterly DPCs. Pair 3 is wrong: the Manipur High Court ordered notional promotions for police officers delayed over a decade, while it was the Himachal Pradesh High Court (2025) that sought faster DPCs for senior lecturers.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 34-36

questions.q:
Under the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026, consider the following pairs:
Law : Change made
1. Delhi Police Act, 1978 : Offence of giving a false fire alarm omitted
2. Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957 : Offence of failing to report births and deaths omitted
3. National Highways Act : Monetary penalty in place of imprisonment for making a highway impassable
4. New Delhi municipal law : A new advertisement tax introduced
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Bill omits petty offences such as a false fire alarm under the Delhi Police Act and failure to report births and deaths under the Delhi municipal law, and replaces jail with a penalty of up to Rs 1 crore for making a national highway impassable. Pair 4 is wrong: for New Delhi the Bill restructures property tax into building and vacant-land taxes and removes the advertisement tax rather than adding one.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 5-7; Shankar IAS pp. 24-25

questions.q:
Arrange the following Acts in the order in which they were enacted, earliest first:
1. Judges (Inquiry) Act
2. Census Act
3. Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act now in force
4. Delimitation Act now in force
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Census Act came first, in 1948, giving the Census its statutory footing after Independence. The Judges (Inquiry) Act of 1968 sets the procedure for investigating charges against higher-court judges. The Delimitation Act of 2002 set up the most recent Commission, and the 2026 Bill that would have replaced it was withdrawn. The current Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act dates from 2010, replacing the 1976 law, and was the subject of an amendment Bill introduced in 2026.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 7-9, 12; Shankar IAS pp. 3-6, 32-34

questions.q:
The April 2026 debate on executive tenure revisited the anti-defection law. With reference to the Tenth Schedule, consider the following statements:
1. A member may be held to have voluntarily given up membership of his party from his conduct, even without a formal resignation.
2. Members escape disqualification on a merger if one-third of the legislature party agree to it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: paragraph 2(1)(a) disqualifies a member who voluntarily gives up party membership, and the Supreme Court has held that this can be inferred from conduct, not only from a formal resignation. Statement 2 is wrong: paragraph 4 protects members in a merger only when at least two-thirds of the legislature party agree; the old one-third split exception was deleted by the 91st Amendment in 2003. Critics in 2026 proposed exempting confidence votes from the whip rule to restore Parliament's daily check.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 30-32; Tenth Schedule paragraphs are static

questions.q:
In the 2026 debate on contempt of court after the NCERT textbook episode, the views of several judges were recalled. Consider the following pairs:
Judge : View on contempt
1. CJI P.B. Gajendragadkar : Contempt power should be used freely to deter any criticism of judges
2. CJI S.P. Bharucha : A 'broad-shouldered' approach that declined to punish critical public figures
3. Lord Denning : Contempt is the proper tool to uphold the personal dignity of judges
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 2 is correct: Bharucha took a broad-shouldered view and refused contempt against critics. Pair 1 is wrong because Gajendragadkar urged that the power be used cautiously and sparingly, warning that impulsive use harms the courts' own dignity. Pair 3 is wrong because Denning said courts should not use contempt to protect their own dignity or silence critics; respect must be earned by conduct. The common thread is that the judiciary, lacking purse and sword, rests on public confidence.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 27-30
